title: HC-HMP: Healthy Choices Implementation Trial
official: Scaling Up Integrated Youth Alcohol and HIV Prevention Interventions: The Healthy Choices Implementation Trial
summary: This study is a national, fully virtual Type 3 hybrid implementation-effectiveness clinical trial using the Multiphase Optimization Strategy (MOST) to evaluate implementation strategies designed to optimize delivery of the Healthy Choices (HC) behavioral intervention through the HealthMpowerment (HMP) digital health platform. A total of 360 emerging adults ages 18-29 who are eligible for antiretroviral therapy (ART) or pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and report recent alcohol use will be randomized using a factorial design to combinations of three implementation strategies: a personalized video introduction to an HC peer counselor, tailored digital messaging, and asynchronous support from an HC counselor. All participants receive HC-HMP. The primary implementation outcome is HC direct-to-consumer fidelity, measured by the number of HC counseling sessions completed. Secondary outcomes include HMP fidelity assessed using platform-generated paradata, alcohol use, and HIV transmission risk. Participants complete assessments at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18-29 years
* Resident of the United States
* Able to read and understand English
* Self-reported as eligible for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) or antiretroviral therapy (ART)
* Self-reported alcohol use within the past 30 days
* Regular access to an internet-connected smartphone capable of supporting the HMP mobile application (Android version 7.0 or higher or iPhone iOS version 16.4 or higher)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Pregnant at the time of screening
* Currently incarcerated
* Unable to provide legally effective informed consent
* Self-reported unmanaged moderate-to-severe mental health symptoms or concerns that would interfere with safe study participation, including active psychosis
* Active heavy illegal drug use that is unmanaged/not currently in treatment, as defined by the study eligibility screener
* Moderate-to-severe suicide risk, including suicidal ideation with plan, as defined by study eligibility and safety procedures
